plot: At sunset in the snowy garden Max finds a hundred tiny footprints; Dog guesses a tiny snow giant and Bird sees them circle the tree, but Max reads the clues himself (three toes, hop-gaps = a baby bird), finds lost chick Pip, then follows the prints backwards to Grandma's bird house where Pip's mama is waiting.

beats.say: Whoa, whoa, WHOA! Slippery snow! Wait a minute... what are these?
The sun is going down. The snowy garden is pink and orange.
And all over the white snow, there are tiny, tiny footprints.
One, two, three... ten... fifty... There must be a hundred tiny footprints here!
Footprints? Let me see! Sniff, sniff. Hmm. They smell like... snow.
Everything here smells like snow, Dog. But who made them?
I know! A snow giant! A very, very tiny snow giant!
A tiny giant? Dog, giants are big. That is why they are called giants.
Oh. Right. Then a tiny snow... not-giant?
Hello, hello! What are we looking at? Treasure?
Footprints, Bird. Can you fly up high and see where they go?
Easy peasy, lemon squeezy! Up, up, up I go!
Bird flies high above the garden and looks down.
Max! The footprints go round and round the big tree. Then they go into the bushes!
Round and round? The tiny not-giant is dizzy! Like me after I chase my tail!
Max! Dog! It will be dark soon. What are you doing out there?
Grandma, we found a mystery! A hundred tiny footprints!
You are a clever cat, Max. Look very closely, and the snow will tell you.
Max bends down close. He looks at one footprint. Then the next one.
Hmm. Each print has three thin toes, like a little fork. Not a cat. Not a dog.
Not a dog? Good. My feet are big and round, and I am right here.
And look. No prints in between. Hop... space... hop... space. Whoever made these, they hop!
Three toes and hopping? That sounds like me! But I was in my nest all afternoon.
Then it is a bird. But why would a bird hop and not fly?
Max thinks and thinks. His tail curls up like a big question mark.
I know! A baby bird! Baby birds cannot fly yet, so they have to hop everywhere!
A baby bird? All alone in the cold snow? We have to find it!
So they follow the tiny footprints. Round the big tree. Past the old stump. Into the bushes.
Peep... peep... is somebody there? Hello?
Hello, little one. Don't be scared. I am Max. What is your name?
I am Pip. I hopped and hopped to see the snow. Now I cannot find my home.
Oh, poor little Pip! Where is your home? In a tree? Under a roof?
I don't know. Everything is white now. Everything looks the same.
Don't worry, Pip! I can dig in the snow and find it!
Wait, Dog. No digging. I have a better idea. The footprints!
The footprints? But they only brought us here, to Pip.
Yes! But footprints go two ways. If we follow them back to where they start, we find where Pip came from!
Oh, what a clever cat! Walk them backwards, Max. I will come with you.
So everybody follows the tiny footprints back. Out of the bushes. Round the big tree. Round and round.
Round and round again! Max, now I am the dizzy one!
And then the footprints stop. Right next to Grandma's little red bird house on the old stump.
My bird house! I put it there last spring. So that is where you live, little Pip!
Home! My home! Mama is inside. I can hear her singing for me!
Bird gently helps Pip hop up, up, up, and into the warm little bird house.
There you go, Pip. Warm and safe. Next time, see the snow with a grown-up, okay?
Okay! Thank you, Max! Thank you, Dog! Thank you, Bird! Peep peep!
Max, you solved the mystery all by yourself. You did not even need my nose!
Thank you, Dog. Grandma was right. If you look closely, the snow tells you the whole story.
Now it is getting dark. Who wants warm milk and cookies by the fire?
Me! Me! I will make the biggest footprints all the way to the door!
So they walk home through the pink evening snow. Big prints, round prints, and little hop prints from Bird.
Tomorrow I will make a hundred footprints that spell my name. M... A... X!
Max, your name only has three letters!
Then I will make three hundred footprints! Big ones!
